Lower sugar: use 70 g sugar. Sugar drops from about 23% to 18%; it sets harder and icier and needs one or two re-spins.
Smoky panna: char the mangoes directly over the gas flame instead of boiling, for a deeper flavour.
recipes.shop_note: Raw mango: Blinkit/Zepto or any sabziwala, March–June. Roasted jeera powder: MDH or Everest, or roast and pound your own.

recipes.title: Watermelon Lime Sorbet
recipes.subtitle: Three ingredients, no cooking, pure summer
recipes.respin: Often 1 re-spin with 1 tbsp water or juice
recipes.intro: If you make one sorbet, start here. Ripe tarbooz, a squeeze of lime and a little sugar is all it takes, and the Blast does the work in under a minute.

ingredients.note: optional; makes the melon taste sweeter

steps.text: Blend watermelon, sugar, lime juice and salt in the Ninja Blast 45–60 seconds until smooth and the sugar dissolves.
Rest 2 minutes so the foam settles, then pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Flatten any hump and run SORBET. Watermelon is watery: if it looks snowy, add 1 tbsp water and RE-SPIN.
Serve at once with a thin lime wheel or a pinch of chaat masala.

tips: Pick a heavy melon with a creamy-yellow ground spot. If yours is pale or bland, add 1 extra tbsp sugar to avoid an icy sorbet.
Pick out every black seed before blending; crushed seeds turn the sorbet grey and gritty.
Leftovers: flatten the top, refreeze, and re-spin before serving.
swaps: Lower sugar: halve the sugar to 35 g. Sugar drops from about 20% to 13%, giving a firmer, granita-like texture that needs two re-spins.
Watermelon mint: blend in 10 mint leaves, or swap the lime for 1 tbsp fresh ginger juice.
Tarbooz chaat: sprinkle each scoop with kala namak, chaat masala and a pinch of chilli powder.
recipes.shop_note: Everything is at any kirana or on Blinkit/Zepto; watermelon is best March–June.

recipes.title: Muzaffarpur Litchi Sorbet
recipes.subtitle: Floral, juicy, gone in minutes
recipes.respin: Rarely needed; if crumbly, re-spin once with 1 tbsp water
recipes.intro: Muzaffarpur's shahi litchis have a season of barely a month, and this is the best way to make it last. The pale, perfumed sorbet tastes like biting into the fruit.

ingredients.note: keeps it pale; lifts the flavour

steps.text: Peel and seed the litchis, scraping off the bitter brown skin that clings to the seed.
Blend the litchi flesh, sugar, water, lime juice and rose water in the Ninja Blast 60 seconds until smooth.
Rest 2 minutes for the foam to settle. Strain for a silkier sorbet, then pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Flatten any hump and run SORBET. Only if powdery, add 1 tbsp water and RE-SPIN.
Serve small scoops with a few chopped fresh litchis or a single mint leaf.

tips: Peeled litchi browns and loses its scent within hours. Blend and freeze the same day, and don't skip the lime.
Litchis are about 15% sugar, so the 60 g added here lands the base near 24%, which scoops beautifully.
Leftovers: flatten the top, refreeze, and re-spin before serving.
swaps: Canned: blend the drained fruit of a 565 g tin, 150 ml of its syrup, the lime and 30 g sugar.
Lower sugar: cut sugar to 30 g. Sugar drops from about 24% to 19%; it freezes firmer and icier and usually needs a re-spin.
Litchi rose: double the rose water and MIX-IN 2 tbsp chopped fresh litchi after spinning, falooda-style.
recipes.shop_note: Fresh litchi: Blinkit/Zepto/BigBasket, late May–June. Canned litchi: Golden Crown on BigBasket or Amazon.

recipes.title: Masala Shikanji Sorbet
recipes.subtitle: Nimbu pani with a frozen kick
recipes.respin: Rarely needed; if crumbly, re-spin once with 1 tbsp water
recipes.intro: Highway dhaba shikanji, with its chaat masala, kala namak and roasted jeera, is a lemon sorbet waiting to happen. Tart, salty and sweet with fresh mint, it makes a sharp finish to a heavy Sunday lunch.

ingredients.note: if gluten-free, check hing isn't wheat-based

steps.text: Warm the sugar with 100 ml water, stirring, just until it dissolves and turns clear. Don't boil it down.
Off heat, add the remaining 160 ml chilled water and cool fully to room temperature.
Blend the cooled syrup with lemon juice, chaat masala, kala namak, jeera, mint and pepper in the Ninja Blast 30 seconds.
Taste and adjust salt or lemon, then pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Flatten any hump and run SORBET. Only if powdery, add 1 tbsp water and RE-SPIN.
Scoop into small glasses with a pinch of chaat masala and a mint sprig.

tips: Lemon sorbet needs more added sugar than fruit sorbets because the juice has almost none. About 22% keeps it scoopable; much less gives lemon ice.
Roll the lemons hard before cutting for more juice, and strain out every seed; one crushed seed tastes bitter.
Leftovers: flatten the top, refreeze, and re-spin before serving.
swaps: Lower sugar: use 70 g. Sugar drops from about 22% to 17%, so expect a harder, icier sorbet, closer to a gola; re-spin once or twice.
Gur shikanji: replace half the sugar with grated jaggery for a darker, caramel-tinged scoop.
Shikanji float: drop a scoop into chilled soda with a pinch of kala namak.
recipes.shop_note: Everything is at any kirana or on Blinkit/Zepto. Chaat masala and roasted jeera: MDH, Everest or Catch.

recipes.title: Nagpur Santra Sorbet
recipes.subtitle: Winter oranges, fresh-squeezed, extra zest
recipes.respin: Rarely needed; if crumbly, re-spin once with 1 tbsp juice
recipes.intro: When Nagpur santras flood the thelas in winter, squeeze a bagful and freeze the sunshine. A quick zest syrup brings the aroma of a freshly peeled orange; the juice keeps it bright and tangy.

steps.text: Zest one orange before cutting, then squeeze all the oranges and strain out the seeds. Measure 340 ml juice.
Warm the sugar, water and zest, stirring, until the sugar dissolves. Off heat, steep 10 minutes.
Cool the zest syrup completely to room temperature before it goes into the Blast.
Blend the syrup, orange juice, lime juice and salt in the Ninja Blast 30 seconds. Rest 1–2 minutes; pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Flatten any hump and run SORBET. If powdery, add 1 tbsp juice and RE-SPIN.
Serve in scooped-out orange halves or small bowls, topped with a curl of zest.

tips: Freeze the base within 30 minutes of squeezing; some Indian oranges turn bitter as the juice sits. Don't press the pith hard.
If your juice tastes sour on its own, add 1 extra tbsp sugar to the syrup so the sorbet stays scoopable.
Leftovers: flatten the top, refreeze, and re-spin before serving.
swaps: Off-season: use 340 ml chilled 100% orange juice (Tropicana or Real Activ, no added sugar), still with the fresh-zest syrup.
Lower sugar: use 40 g sugar. Sugar drops from about 21% to 16%, giving a firmer, icier sorbet that needs one or two re-spins.
Orange-ginger: steep 1 tsp grated fresh ginger in the syrup with the zest, then strain.
recipes.shop_note: Nagpur oranges: Blinkit/Zepto/BigBasket and local thelas, November–March. Otherwise use kinnow or any sweet orange.

recipes.title: Dragon Fruit Protein Smoothie Bowl
recipes.subtitle: Hot-pink breakfast with 37 g protein
recipes.intro: Pink-fleshed dragon fruit, now grown across Gujarat and Maharashtra as kamalam, makes a shockingly pink bowl. Banana adds body, Greek yogurt and whey bring the protein, and the CREAMi makes it thick enough for toppings.

ingredients.note: MuscleBlaze, Avvatar or ON; ~24 g protein
optional if your whey is sweet

steps.text: Add milk, yogurt, dragon fruit, banana, honey, whey and xanthan to the Ninja Blast, liquids first. Blend 45–60 seconds until evenly pink.
Rest 2–3 minutes, or tap the vessel, so the whey foam settles. Pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Let the pint sit 5 minutes, flatten any hump, then run SMOOTHIE BOWL.
If crumbly, add 1–2 tbsp milk and RE-SPIN until thick and spoonable.
Divide between two bowls; top with granola, chia or pumpkin seeds, sliced banana, kiwi and coconut flakes.

tips: Dragon fruit is cheapest from monsoon to early winter. Freeze cubed flesh in zip bags and blend it, half-thawed, whenever you want a bowl.
Toppings aren't counted in the nutrition: 30 g granola and 1 tbsp seeds add roughly 180 kcal and 5 g protein.
Leftovers: flatten the top, refreeze, and re-spin with a splash of milk before serving.
swaps: No whey: use 150 g Greek yogurt and skip the milk. Protein falls to about 16 g and the bowl is tangier.
Tropical: swap the banana for 80 g ripe mango and use coconut or unflavoured whey.
Gluten-free: top with seeds, nuts and coconut instead of oat granola, or use certified gluten-free granola.
recipes.shop_note: Pink dragon fruit: Blinkit/Zepto/BigBasket (check 'red flesh'). Xanthan: Urban Platter on Amazon. Granola: Yogabar or True Elements.

recipes.title: Bournvita Malt Protein Thickshake
recipes.subtitle: Tann ki shakti, plus 40 g protein
recipes.respin: LITE ICE CREAM first; re-spin once with 1 tbsp milk if powdery, then MILKSHAKE
recipes.intro: Remember sneaking spoonfuls of dry Bournvita from the jar? This is that taste grown up: a malty chocolate base frozen with whey, spun creamy, then whipped with cold milk into a spoon-thick shake.

ingredients.note: MuscleBlaze, Avvatar or ON; ~24 g protein

steps.text: Blend 320 ml milk, Bournvita, whey, xanthan and salt in the Ninja Blast 45 seconds until no powdery lumps remain.
Rest 2–3 minutes or tap the vessel so the foam settles, then pour into the pint, well under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Flatten any hump and run LITE ICE CREAM. If powdery, add 1 tbsp milk and RE-SPIN once.
Make a 4 cm well to the bottom, pour in the remaining 120 ml milk and run MILKSHAKE.
Pour into two tall glasses, dust with dry Bournvita and serve with a wide straw and a spoon.

tips: Bournvita barely dissolves in cold milk with a spoon, but the Blast handles it in seconds. Scrape out any powder sludge at the bottom.
Want it sweeter? Add 1 tbsp sugar or Milkmaid to the base; it also makes the frozen pint slightly softer.
Leftovers: pour extra shake back into the pint, flatten, refreeze, and process on LITE ICE CREAM before adding milk again.
swaps: Horlicks: use 40 g Classic Malt Horlicks and vanilla whey for a lighter, more biscuity malt.
Boost or Complan work the same way; Boost gives a darker, more chocolatey shake.
Malt-biscuit crunch: after the LITE ICE CREAM spin, run MIX-IN with 2 crushed Parle-G before adding the milk.
recipes.shop_note: Bournvita and Horlicks: any kirana or Blinkit/Zepto. Whey: Amazon, Blinkit or brand sites. Xanthan: Urban Platter on Amazon.

welcome.title: Welcome to Your Creami Kitchen
paragraphs: This book has 50 recipes written for the Ninja CREAMi NC300IN and the Ninja Blast portable blender, using ingredients you can order on Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart, BigBasket or Amazon, or pick up at the kirana. High-protein pints run through the whole book, alongside kulfi-style desi flavours, gelatos and fruit sorbets.

The recipes are split into six sections: Protein Pints: Whey-Powered; Protein Pints: Greek Yogurt, Turbo & Paneer; Desi Ice Creams; Global Classics; Gelato; and Sorbets, Bowls & Shakes. Start with the reference pages that follow. They explain the programs, the sweeteners and the fixes for common texture problems.

Each recipe page shows a program badge (the button to press), a Blast step for blending the base, a 24-hour freeze, the spin and any re-spin. Quantities are metric first, with Indian cups (240 ml) in brackets. Use the notes area to record your freezer's quirks, sweetness changes and the brands you prefer.

how_it_works.text: Add the cold or room-temperature base to the Blast and blend 30–60 s. Cook-and-cool recipes must be fully cool before they go in.
Rest the blended base 2–3 min, or tap the vessel on the counter, so the foam from whey or yogurt subsides.
Pour into a CREAMi pint up to, never above, the MAX FILL line (about 400–450 ml). Lid it and label it with the name and date.
Freeze the pint on a level shelf for a full 24 hours at -13 °C to -22 °C. A slanted pint freezes with an uneven top.
Remove the lid, flatten any hump, lock the pint into the outer bowl and press the program shown on the recipe.
If it looks powdery or crumbly, add 1–2 tbsp milk and press RE-SPIN. Lite and protein bases often need one or two.
Dig a 4 cm well, add up to ⅓ cup mix-ins and run MIX-IN. Flatten leftovers, refreeze, and re-spin before serving again.

programs.name: ICE CREAM
programs.best_for: Full-fat bases with cream, milk and sugar or condensed milk
programs.use_when: The base has real sugar and at least some cream

programs.name: LITE ICE CREAM
programs.texture: Soft-serve once re-spun; may start powdery
programs.use_when: Using whey, Greek yogurt, paneer, stevia, sucralose, erythritol or allulose

programs.name: GELATO
programs.use_when: The base was cooked and cooled: gelato, kulfi, rabdi, caramel

programs.name: SORBET
programs.use_when: Mango, jamun, kokum, lemon or watermelon with sugar or syrup

programs.name: SMOOTHIE BOWL
programs.best_for: Frozen fruit with yogurt, juice or milk
programs.use_when: You want a breakfast bowl to top with granola and fruit

programs.name: MILKSHAKE
programs.best_for: A frozen or processed pint plus about 120 ml milk
programs.use_when: Turning a pint (or leftovers) into a shake in about 2 minutes

programs.name: MIX-IN
programs.best_for: Folding in biscuits, nuts, chocolate or ripples
programs.use_when: The pint is already processed and a 4 cm well is dug to the bottom

programs.name: RE-SPIN
programs.best_for: Rescuing powdery, crumbly or too-cold results
programs.use_when: After any program, with 1–2 tbsp milk added; repeat if needed

blast.intro: The Ninja Blast holds 530 ml with a practical max fill of about 470 ml, so one full pint base blends in a single go. It is cordless and charges by USB-C.
dos: Blend cold or room-temperature bases for 30–60 s, or 2–3 blend cycles.
Add liquids first, then powders (whey, cocoa, gum), then soft solids.
Rest whey and yogurt bases 2–3 min so foam settles before pouring.
Sprinkle xanthan or guar gum over moving liquid to avoid lumps.
Charge it fully before a batch day; one charge covers several pints.
donts: Never blend hot liquids: the sealed vessel builds pressure.
Don't grind hard nuts, ice or whole spices on their own.
Don't knead thick doughs or very dense pastes without liquid.
Don't submerge the motor base in water; rinse only the jar and lid.

golden_rules.title: Freeze a full 24 hours
golden_rules.text: A part-frozen core gives soupy, uneven results. Plan one day ahead.

golden_rules.title: Respect MAX FILL
golden_rules.text: Overfilled pints can jam or damage the machine. Keep bases at about 400–450 ml.

golden_rules.title: Freeze level
golden_rules.text: Set pints on a flat shelf away from the door. A slanted top strains the blade.

golden_rules.title: Flatten the hump
golden_rules.text: If the top freezes domed, rest 5–10 min or scrape it flat with a spoon before spinning.

golden_rules.title: Powdery is normal
golden_rules.text: Lite and protein pints often come out crumbly first. Add 1–2 tbsp milk and re-spin.

golden_rules.title: Never cook whey
golden_rules.text: Heat makes whey grainy and clumpy. Blend it into a cold or cooled base.

golden_rules.title: Keep whey to 1–1.5 scoops
golden_rules.text: 30–45 g per pint is the sweet spot; more turns chalky and icy.

golden_rules.title: Use a pinch of gum
golden_rules.text: ⅛–¼ tsp xanthan or guar gum makes low-fat bases noticeably creamier.

golden_rules.title: Cool before you Blast
golden_rules.text: Cooked bases for gelato, kulfi or chai must reach room temperature before blending.

golden_rules.title: Mix-ins go in last
golden_rules.text: Add them after processing, into a 4 cm well, and use MIX-IN, never the main program.

protein_guide.intro: Protein sources freeze differently. Fat-free and high-protein bases freeze harder, so expect a re-spin and add a pinch of gum. Figures are typical label values; check your pack.

rows.tip: Add gum + 1 tbsp cream or SMP
Thickens on standing; add 2–3 tbsp extra milk
Balance tang with honey or fruit

rows.texture: Very thick, fat-free, firm when frozen
rows.tip: Thin with milk; plan one re-spin
Crumble and blend with milk until fully smooth
Use as the liquid; sweetness is already low

sweetener_guide.name: Sugar
sweetener_guide.tip: Grind to caster so it dissolves in cold bases

sweetener_guide.name: Condensed milk (Milkmaid)
sweetener_guide.freeze_effect: Soft and creamy, adds milk solids
sweetener_guide.tip: About 100 g sweetens a pint; whisk in first

sweetener_guide.name: Honey / jaggery
sweetener_guide.freeze_effect: Softer than sugar; jaggery adds caramel notes
sweetener_guide.tip: Add jaggery to warm, not boiling, milk to avoid curdling

sweetener_guide.name: Sucralose / aspartame (Sugar Free Natura / Gold)
sweetener_guide.freeze_effect: No softening; freezes hard and powdery
sweetener_guide.tip: Add to cold bases (aspartame loses sweetness with heat); plan a re-spin

sweetener_guide.name: Stevia (Sugar Free Green)
sweetener_guide.tip: Use less than you think; vanilla masks the aftertaste

sweetener_guide.name: Erythritol / monk fruit blends
sweetener_guide.tip: Mix with allulose; eat within a week

sweetener_guide.name: Allulose
sweetener_guide.freeze_effect: Softer than sugar, like a regular ice cream
sweetener_guide.tip: Best sugar-free option for scoopable pints

sweetener_guide.name: Dates
sweetener_guide.tip: Soak in hot water 15 min, cool, then Blast with the milk

troubleshooting.why: Low fat or sugar, or a very cold freezer
troubleshooting.fix: Add 1–2 tbsp milk and RE-SPIN; repeat once if needed

troubleshooting.why: Too much water, too little fat, sugar or solids
troubleshooting.fix: Add SMP, cream or a pinch of gum next time

troubleshooting.why: Too much sugar, honey or allulose, or freezer too warm
troubleshooting.fix: Refreeze 1–2 h; reduce sweetener; check freezer is -18 °C

troubleshooting.why: Base expanded as it froze; pint not level
troubleshooting.fix: Rest 5–10 min or scrape flat before spinning

troubleshooting.why: Added without a well, or too many
troubleshooting.fix: Dig a 4 cm well to the bottom; max ⅓ cup; use MIX-IN

troubleshooting.why: Whey or yogurt whipped air into the base
troubleshooting.fix: Rest 2–3 min or tap the Blast before pouring

troubleshooting.why: Too much whey, or isolate with no fat
troubleshooting.fix: Stay at 1–1.5 scoops; add 2 tbsp cream or SMP

troubleshooting.problem: Machine won't start / bowl won't lock
troubleshooting.why: Lid, bowl or pint not seated and twisted fully
troubleshooting.fix: Twist the outer bowl until it clicks; check the paddle is fitted

troubleshooting.why: Pint refroze solid after the first spin
troubleshooting.fix: Flatten the top, add 1 tbsp milk, run the program again

troubleshooting.why: Whey heated, or acidic fruit added to hot milk
troubleshooting.fix: Cool bases first; add fruit and whey cold

storage: Flatten the surface of leftovers with a spoon, lid tightly and refreeze; re-spin before serving again.
Plain dairy pints keep best for 2–3 weeks; protein, sugar-free and sorbet pints for 1–2 weeks.
Refreeze a pint only once or twice; repeated thawing makes it icy.
Label every lid with recipe name, date and program; masking tape and a marker work well.
Keep pints at the back of a level shelf, away from the door, at about -18 °C.
shopping_tips: Keep a standing basket of milk, cream, Milkmaid, cocoa, whey and xanthan, so a pint takes one reorder.
Order cream and Greek yogurt last, check the expiry date on delivery, and refrigerate straight away.
Check marshmallows, sprinkles and jelly sweets for the FSSAI green dot; many imported ones contain gelatin.
Buy specialty items such as xanthan gum, pistachio paste and vanilla extract from Urban Platter on Amazon.
Buy mango pulp tins in May–June when stock is fresh, and freeze seasonal fruit pulp in pint-sized batches.
Compare whey per-scoop protein on the label, not the pack size; flavoured tubs vary widely.
